cases.prompt:
Implement a pure Python function summarize(lines) that consumes strings in the log format below and returns a dictionary mapping route names to dictionaries with integer keys "count", "errors", and "max_latency_ms". Count a status >= 400 as an error. Route is the path immediately after the HTTP method, not the method itself. Ignore malformed lines rather than raising. Treat latency as a nonnegative integer and reject records missing any field. Support an empty input. Do not use global state or mutate the input. Return only a Python code block containing the function.

The source is a tiny gateway, and duplicate lines represent separate requests. The status may be any three-digit integer; a route contains no spaces. The columns can have leading and trailing whitespace around vertical-bar separators. There is no need to compute averages or percentages. Lines with a missing status or noninteger latency are malformed and ignored.

cases.prompt:
Write a pure Python function order_jobs(deps) for a build scheduler. deps is a dictionary mapping each job name to an iterable of prerequisite names. Return a list containing every named job exactly once, with each prerequisite before its dependent. Include prerequisite names even if absent as keys. Among all currently runnable names choose the lexicographically smallest. If there is any cycle, raise ValueError. Do not modify deps or its iterables. Return only a Python code block containing the function.

This is used to plan small test builds; no durations, owners, priority weights, concurrency, or network calls belong in the function. Input names are nonempty strings. A job can list the same prerequisite more than once; that duplicate must not make a valid graph fail. Self dependencies are cycles. Unrelated jobs remain deterministic. A reference workload follows, with duration and owner recorded for humans only:

job-01: depends=[]; duration=8; owner=db
job-02: depends=[job-01]; duration=6; owner=ops
job-03: depends=[job-02]; duration=4; owner=ui
job-04: depends=[job-03, job-02]; duration=2; owner=api
job-05: depends=[job-04]; duration=9; owner=db
job-06: depends=[job-05]; duration=7; owner=ops
job-07: depends=[job-06]; duration=5; owner=ui
job-08: depends=[job-07, job-06]; duration=3; owner=api
job-09: depends=[job-08]; duration=1; owner=db
job-10: depends=[job-09]; duration=8; owner=ops
job-11: depends=[job-10]; duration=6; owner=ui
job-12: depends=[job-11, job-10]; duration=4; owner=api
job-13: depends=[job-12]; duration=2; owner=db
job-14: depends=[job-13]; duration=9; owner=ops
job-15: depends=[job-14]; duration=7; owner=ui
job-16: depends=[job-15, job-14]; duration=5; owner=api
job-17: depends=[job-16]; duration=3; owner=db
job-18: depends=[job-17]; duration=1; owner=ops
job-19: depends=[job-18]; duration=8; owner=ui

Examples: order_jobs({}) returns []; order_jobs({"c": ["a", "b"], "a": []}) returns ["a", "b", "c"]; order_jobs({"a": ["b"], "b": ["a"]}) raises ValueError; order_jobs({"b": ["a", "a"]}) returns ["a", "b"].
checks: Missing prerequisite keys are included and lexicographically ordered.
Duplicate edges do not block a job.
